questions.e: Opposite moments cancel.

questions.e: Subtract opposite moments; the greater clockwise moment determines direction.

questions.q: Which object is more stable on a table?
o: A cone balanced on its tip
questions.e: Wide base and low centre of mass increase stability.

questions.q: Why is it easier to move a heavy cabinet using rollers?
o: Rolling friction is less than sliding friction
questions.e: Rollers replace sliding contact with lower rolling resistance.

questions.q: Why can brakes become hot after repeated stopping?
o: Friction dissipates kinetic energy as heat
questions.e: Braking friction transforms mechanical energy into thermal energy.

questions.q: At the instant a falling skydiver reaches terminal velocity, acceleration is:
questions.e: Balanced drag and weight give zero acceleration.

questions.q: Before reaching terminal velocity, as air resistance increases, a falling object’s acceleration generally:
questions.e: Growing upward drag reduces the net downward force.

questions.q: When a stone is whirled in a horizontal circle, the string force points:
questions.e: String tension provides inward centripetal force.

questions.q: If the orbital radius stays fixed but the orbital period doubles, average orbital speed:
questions.e: v = 2πr/T, so speed is inversely proportional to period.

questions.q: If orbital radius doubles while orbital period is unchanged, average orbital speed:
questions.e: v = 2πr/T for a circular path.

questions.q: A lamina is suspended from two points in turn. Its centre of gravity lies:

questions.e: The centre of gravity lies on each suspension vertical.

questions.q: A spinning fan slows after switching off because:

questions.e: Large perpendicular lever arm gives the greatest torque.

questions.q: For a body at rest on a table, its upward normal force balances its:

questions.e: Equal forces need equal moment arms for opposite torques to cancel.

questions.q: What is the direction of acceleration for uniform circular motion?
questions.e: Velocity changes direction toward the circle centre.
